# The chemistry lines — for a profile, for a room, and for you in a room

**Written 2026-10-03 for `MVP_INSTRUCTIONS.md` §4.** Six factors × nine combinations of
*(your pole, their pole)*. Generated by `simulations/pairchem.py`; this document is the copy.

**Rules the copy follows.**

- **Written to the viewer, about the person whose profile is open.** "You" is the reader; "they"
  is the other person. Never "this user".
- **One sentence.** Two at the absolute most, and only where the second earns it.
- **It says what will happen, not what you are.** *"They'll still be going when you're done"* beats
  *"you have different energy levels."*
- **A difference is never a warning.** Opposites are stated as a fact about the night, and often as
  the reason it works.
- **No jargon, no factor names, no numbers.** The user never sees `ENRG`.

**Poles.** `high` = 70 and above · `mid` = 31–69 · `low` = 30 and below.

---

## `ENRG` — how hard you go

| you | them | the line |
|---|---|---|
| high | high | **Neither of you is going home early.** |
| high | mid | **You'll set the pace, and they'll come along.** |
| high | low | **You want it louder than they do — expect to be the one pushing.** |
| mid | high | **They'll take the night further than you planned it.** |
| mid | mid | **Neither of you is pushing. It'll go where it goes.** |
| mid | low | **They'll keep it gentler than you might have.** |
| low | high | **They'll still be going long after you're done.** |
| low | mid | **You'll be the reason it stays easy.** |
| low | low | **A calm night, and you both actually want one.** |

| you | them | the line |
|---|---|---|
| high | high | **You'll find a table and stay at it, and that's the night.** |
| high | mid | **You'll be the one keeping everyone together.** |
| high | low | **You want your people; they want the room. Two nights happening at one table.** |
| mid | high | **They'll keep the group together without being asked.** |
| mid | mid | **Neither of you minds much where you end up sitting.** |
| mid | low | **They'll be the one talking to strangers.** |
| low | high | **They'll hold the table while you work the room.** |
| low | mid | **You'll be the one talking to strangers.** |
| low | low | **Neither of you is sitting still. You'll know half the room by midnight.** |

| low | high | **They came out to talk. You came out for the noise.** |
| low | mid | **You won't mind at all if it gets loud.** |
| low | low | **Neither of you needs to hear a word. Go somewhere loud.** |

| mid | low | **They'd rather nothing was on.** |
| low | high | **They want something on. You'd rather it was just the two of you.** |
| low | mid | **You'd rather nothing was on.** |
| low | low | **No stage, no act, nothing to face. You two are the night.** |

|---|---|---|

| you | them | the line |

| mid | mid | **It'll get sorted at some point.** |
| mid | low | **They'll be the one who books.** |

---

# The headlines

**Computed from the shape of the whole read, not from any one factor.** Shown above the lines.

| headline | fires when |
|---|---|
| **Same wavelength** | three or more of the top factors land on the same pole for both of you |
| **Two different nights** | two or more of the splitting factors — who you face, whether you dance — are firmly opposed |
| **Aligned, with one split** | mostly together, and one real difference |
| **You'll carry this one** | three or more of the top factors are led by you and none by them |
| **They'll carry this one** | the mirror of it |
| **You'll trade off** | you each lead on something |
| **Nobody's pushing** | four or more factors flat on both sides |
| **Push and pull** | everything else |

**The thresholds are guesses** and should be re-tuned once there are real pairs to look at rather
than invented ones.

---

# Three rules for whoever edits these

**Never make a difference sound like a problem.** *"You'll dance and they'll hold the table — that's
a good arrangement"* is the tone. The app is not a compatibility test.

**Never let a line be true of everybody.** If a sentence would read fine against any other pole
combination, it is not saying anything. The mid/mid lines are the ones most at risk, which is why
several of them are deliberately short — a flat axis genuinely has little to say, and padding it
would be worse than admitting it.

**The low/low lines are the hardest and the most valuable.** Two people who both want the quiet,
seated, unplanned version of a night are a real and under-served pair, and the lines for them
should never read as the absence of energy. *"A calm night, and you both actually want one"* is the
model.

---

# The room line (2026-10-07)

**Every room shown to a user carries one sentence about what it is.** Generated by
`simulations/roomline.py` from the room vector `CHEMISTRY_V4` already produces — **no new engine,
and nothing extra to collect.**

> **This room has a chill vibe, and they want to see how the night unfolds rather than stick to a
> plan.**

### How it is chosen

**The same two-factor selection as the daily name**, rendered as prose rather than as two words: the
factor furthest from the middle leads, and a second joins if it clears `SECOND_MIN` 20 while staying
within `STICKY` 15 of the first.

**With one deliberate difference. The line ranks on `weight × distance`; the name ranks on distance
alone.** Naming dropped the weights on 2026-09-23 and that is still right for a name — but a
*description* is a different job, and **the weights encode how much an axis matters to how a night
feels.** A room at `ENRG` 23 and `SPONT` 84 is further from the middle on `SPONT`, but *chill* is the
truer headline than *unplanned*:

| ranked like the name | **This room is deciding it on the night, and nobody is trying to push it harder.** |
|---|---|
| **ranked by weight × distance** | **This room has a chill vibe, and they want to see how the night unfolds rather than stick to a plan.** |

**So the line and the name can disagree on which factor leads.** That is accepted: they answer
different questions, and the second reading is the one a person recognises.

### A split outranks a second factor

When `AFFIL` or `MOVE` splits, that clause takes the second slot. **It is the most useful thing the
model knows about a room and the name cannot say it at all** — a name has one pole per factor and a
split has two.

### The clauses

**Leading** — *"This room…"*

| | low | high |
|---|---|---|
| `ENRG` | has a chill vibe | is going hard tonight |
| `AFFIL` | is here to meet the room | is here for its own table |
| `TALK` | wants it loud | came to talk |
| `FOCUS` | is its own main event | is here for whatever is on |
| `MOVE` | is settling in somewhere | is going to be on its feet |
| `SPONT` | has tonight planned | is deciding it on the night |

**Second** — *"…, and…"*

| | low | high |
|---|---|---|
| `ENRG` | nobody is trying to push it harder | nobody is planning an early night |
| `AFFIL` | they will end up talking to strangers | they will mostly keep to themselves |
| `TALK` | you will not hear much over the music | the conversation is the point |
| `FOCUS` | they are not looking for a show | they will want to be near the front |
| `MOVE` | they will want somewhere to sit | they will want somewhere to dance |
| `SPONT` | they would rather know where they are going | they want to see how the night unfolds rather than stick to a plan |

**Split** — takes the second slot when it fires

| `AFFIL` | some will hold the table while others work the room |
|---|---|
| `MOVE` | it needs a floor and somewhere to sit |

### The flat room

**A room where nothing clears 12 points from the middle gets no invented character.**

> **This room has not decided what it is yet — nobody in it is pushing in any direction.**

That is a real state and it is worth saying: five people with no strong feelings produce a room with
no shape, and claiming otherwise would be the engine making something up.

### The rules are the same as the 54

Written to the viewer. One sentence. Says what will happen, not what people are. **A difference is
never a warning.** No jargon, no factor names, no numbers.

# You in a room (2026-10-07)

**The read a person gets before deciding whether to join.** `roomline.py` says what a room *is*;
this says what *you* would be in it. Generated by `simulations/roomfit.py` — again no new engine,
because `chem4.py` already produces every input.

### The headline uses two numbers, because they answer different questions

`match` is how close you are to the room's identity. `disturbance` is how much the room moves when
you join. **They were measured and they come apart** — `CHEMISTRY_V4.md` §9 puts the correlation at
**r = −0.59**, with only **40%** of the best-matched rooms also among the least-disturbed.

**Why:** disturbance depends on the room's *structure*, not on your similarity. **A room of neutrals
is moved by anybody, however well matched; a room already firm on both poles is saturated and cannot
be moved at all, however badly matched.**

| | disturbance low | disturbance mid | disturbance high |
|---|---|---|---|
| **match high** | YOU WOULD SLOT STRAIGHT IN | YOUR KIND OF ROOM | YOUR KIND OF ROOM, AND YOU WOULD SET THE TONE |
| **match mid** | YOU WOULD BARELY CHANGE THIS ROOM | YOU WOULD FIND YOUR PLACE | YOU WOULD MOVE THIS ROOM |
| **match low** | THIS IS THEIR NIGHT, AND IT WILL NOT BEND | A DIFFERENT NIGHT FROM YOURS | YOU WOULD CHANGE THIS ROOM |

**A split overrides all nine:** *THERE IS A HALF OF THIS ROOM FOR YOU*. When the room holds both
poles there is no single answer to how you fit, and pretending otherwise would be the one dishonest
headline available.

Thresholds: match **0.80 / 0.70**, disturbance **0.090 / 0.047** — the terciles of the post-2026-10-07 distribution over 6,000 joins. **They were re-cut twice:** the first attempt used figures from a preview model that still double-counted mid members, and put only 11% of reads in the low band where they should hold about a third.
**Disturbance must be size-normalised before it is banded** — a joiner moves a pair far more than a
room of five, and the raw number is not comparable across sizes.

### The axis lines — three relations, not nine

A room is a *level*, not a person, so the useful statement is directional: **is the room above you on
this axis, level with you, or below.** Eighteen lines rather than fifty-four.

| | the room is above you | level | the room is below you |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ENRG` | They will take this further than you would have. | You are pitched where they are, so nobody is dragging anybody. | You will be the one pushing this room along. |
| `AFFIL` | They will stay at their own table longer than you would. | You face the night the same way they do. | They will be off meeting people while you would rather hold the table. |
| `TALK` | They came to talk. You would take it louder than this. | You and they want the same volume. | It will be louder than you would have picked, so do not plan on talking. |
| `FOCUS` | They are here for whatever is on. You would be fine without it. | You want the same amount of main event as they do. | They are the event themselves. You would have liked something to watch. |
| `MOVE` | They will be on their feet before you are. | You will be standing and sitting at the same times they are. | You will be the first one up. |
| `SPONT` | They are deciding it as it goes. You would rather have it set. | You and they want the same amount of plan. | They have it planned. You would have left it looser. |

**Above or below starts at 18 points.** Inside that you are pitched the same.

**Which lines show:** at most three, ranked by `weight × gap` — the axes that matter most, where you
differ most. A split always takes the first slot.

### Split lines

| `AFFIL` you high | There is a table in this room, and it is yours. |
|---|---|
| `AFFIL` you low | Half this room is working the floor. That half is yours. |
| `AFFIL` you mid | This room is in two halves and you are not firmly in either — take whichever suits. |
| `MOVE` you high | There is a floor here and people already on it. |
| `MOVE` you low | There is somewhere to sit here, and people sitting. |
| `MOVE` you mid | Some are on the floor and some are sitting. You could take either. |

### Two rules the prototype had to learn

**Never pad a difference with an agreement.** If the top axes genuinely differ, the third slot is not
filled with *"you want the same amount of plan"* — that is noise next to a real finding.

**And when nothing differs, say it once.** A person who matches a room on every axis was getting
three near-identical agreement sentences. **One is stronger than three**, so the all-level case
collapses to a single line.

---

# What chemistry is for, and what it is not (2026-10-14, entry 208)

**The user: "chemistry is a way to match users to rooms in rankings but other than that its job is not
to dictate a night a person has but rather give assessments on how that person would match with the
user they're browsing."**

**Two jobs, and the boundary between them and the third thing matters more than either.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **it ranks rooms** | `match` against the room's identity vector, one half of the room ranking (entry 187). The other half is the user's drawn shape against the room's actual plan |
| **it describes people to each other** | *you and Zoya both…* on a profile, in search, in the friend list, and now in the people ranking (entry 205) |
| **it does NOT decide the night** | **the skeleton does that, alone.** Chemistry has never touched a venue and must not start |

**That third line is the architecture in one sentence and it is the one that drifts**, because every
few weeks something appears that would be slightly better if chemistry were allowed to pick a place.
**Advising how to use a room already chosen is not choosing it** - which is why Plan Insights is
allowed to say *sit at the bar* from `AFFIL` and is not allowed to say *go to this bar*.

---

# The pair readings - two factors that mean something together

**The user: "a person with high focus and high talk means they want to have discussions about the
event they're for, but a person with high focus low talk means they'd rather just have company
undisturbed while they observe the performance."**

**Six single-axis lines say where somebody sits on six scales. A pair reading says what kind of
person that makes them**, and it is information neither line carries alone. **This is the same move
the room line makes - two factors chosen, one sentence - pointed at a person instead of a room.**

**When a pair fires.** Both factors **firm**, which is the band `chem4.strength()` already uses:
**70 or above, or 30 or below.** A mid value on either side means **no reading** - the pair has
nothing to say, and inventing one is how a profile starts lying. **At most two on a profile, three on a chemistry read** — and **ordered by how rare the quadrant is, not by the factors' weights.**

> **Corrected 2026-10-14, the first time these were run.** Weight-ordering surfaced the blandest pair: `ENRG`×`TALK` carries the highest combined weight (32) and says the least — *loud is the point; talking is not* was ranked above *there for the act, and wants company that doesn't talk through it* on the same person. **The two highest-weighted factors pair into the most generic sentence**, because weight measures how much a factor moves a match score, not how much a reading tells you about somebody.
>
> **Rarity is the right sort**: a reading most people would also get tells the viewer nothing. It is the same principle as `SECOND_MIN` in the naming engine, which exists so that half the city is not called the same thing. **Until there is a population to measure rarity against, rank by the two values' combined distance from 50** — firmer is rarer, approximately, and it needs no data.

### `FOCUS` × `TALK` — weight 28

| | |
|---|---|
| **both high** | **there for the act, and wants to talk about it.** The gig is the reason and the conversation is the point of the gig |
| **`FOCUS` high, `TALK` low** | **there for the act, and wants company that doesn't talk through it.** Not unsociable — present, and pointed the same way as you |
| **`FOCUS` low, `TALK` high** | **no main event; the people are the event** |
| **both low** | **there for the room itself**, not for a thing to watch or a conversation to have |

### `AFFIL` × `TALK` — weight 30

| | |
|---|---|
| **both high** | **works the room, and will talk to anyone in it** |
| **`AFFIL` high, `TALK` low** | **likes being among people without having to talk to them.** The crowd is the company |
| **`AFFIL` low, `TALK` high** | **your own table, and a long conversation at it** |
| **both low** | **your own people, and no need to fill the quiet** |

### `ENRG` × `MOVE` — weight 30

| | |
|---|---|
| **both high** | **goes hard, and ends up on the floor** |
| **`ENRG` high, `MOVE` low** | **wants it loud and full, and will watch from the edge.** The intensity is the draw; the dancing is not |
| **`ENRG` low, `MOVE` high** | **wants a floor without a crush** |
| **both low** | **sat down, and happy about it** |

### `ENRG` × `TALK` — weight 32

| | |
|---|---|
| **both high** | **happy to shout over the music** |
| **`ENRG` high, `TALK` low** | **loud is the point; talking is not** |
| **`ENRG` low, `TALK` high** | **quiet enough to actually hear each other** |
| **both low** | **low and easy, parallel company** |

### `SPONT` × `FOCUS` — weight 24

| | |
|---|---|
| **`SPONT` low, `FOCUS` high** | **books for the act and arrives for the set** |
| **both high** | **wants something on, and will take whatever is on tonight** |
| **both low** | **the same table, the same night, planned** |
| **`SPONT` high, `FOCUS` low** | **turns up and sees what happens** |

### `AFFIL` × `MOVE` — weight 28, two quadrants only

| | |
|---|---|
| **both high** | **dances with the room** |
| **`AFFIL` low, `MOVE` high** | **dances with their own people, in a huddle** |

**The other two quadrants are left blank deliberately.** *Outward-facing and seated* and *inward and
seated* are already said better by the `AFFIL` × `TALK` pair, and **a reading that repeats another
reading is worse than no reading.**

### On somebody else's profile: where you agree, and where you do not

**Browsing a person runs both sets and compares them.**

- **a reading you both fire** → *"you both came for the act and want to talk about it"* - the
  strongest thing the screen can say, because it is specific and mutual;
- **the same pair, different quadrants** → *"you want to talk about it; she wants to watch it"* -
  **the most useful line on the screen**, because it is the one that tells somebody what the evening
  would actually feel like;
- **nothing fires on either side** → say nothing. **A profile with no firm pairs is a person who
  is easy tonight**, and the single-axis lines already cover that.

**Why the disagreement line earns its place.** The percentage says *how well you match*; the
disagreement says *in what way you do not*, which is the thing a person is actually trying to work out
when they scroll past somebody. **It is also the honest use of chemistry** - describing two people to
each other, not deciding where they go.

### What this is not

**Not a venue filter.** No pair reading selects, scores or excludes a place. **Not a plan input.** The
skeleton decides the night. **Not a gate on who can be added to a night** - a pair that disagrees is
interesting, not disqualifying, and the whole point of *Table and Floor* as a chemistry tag is that
rooms containing both are real and often good.
